chunks: And through him, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, who said: He narrated to us Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from al-Mufadhdhal ibn Umar, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah: What is the sign of the Qa'im?

He said: When the orbit turns and it is said: Has he died, perished, or which valley has he followed? I said: May I be your ransom, then what will happen? He said: He will not appear except with the sword.

key_terms.السَّيْف: The sword, symbolizing military power and conquest
key_terms.الْفَلَك: The orbit/sphere, referring to the celestial order or the state of affairs
key_terms.الْقَائِم: The Riser, a title for the Mahdi

ai.seo_question: What are the signs preceding the appearance of the Mahdi according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Nu'mani highlights the transition from the Great Occultation to the Mahdi's public emergence, characterized by a period of existential uncertainty where the community questions the Imam's status. The phrase 'which valley has he followed?' reflects the Shia belief in his continued hidden presence before the definitive sign of his appearance 'with the sword,' emphasizing that his rise is not merely political but a divinely ordained restoration of justice through decisive action.
